title: wwcf-weizal-1996-world
label: The Hitman

won.source: The fed's own "Saturday Newsletter" (12 January 1996): "The Hitman won the W.W.C.F. title from Masked Mayhem" at the Providence, Rhode Island house show, 9 January 1996.

how: Defeated champion Masked Mayhem with the Firecracker kick at the fed's first house show, 9 January 1996.
note: Lost the title two days later to The Soul Swiper, 11 January 1996.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-world
label: The Soul Swiper

won.source: The fed's own "Saturday Newsletter" (12 January 1996): "New W.W.C.F. World Champion is The Soul Swiper," from the 11 January 1996 house show at the Rosemary School gymnasium.

how: Pinned champion The Hitman with a heart punch, 11 January 1996.
note: Lost the title back to Masked Mayhem five days later, 16 January 1996.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-world
label: Masked Mayhem

won.source: The fed's own "Friday Newsletter" (21 January 1996): "Masked Mayhem regained the WWCF title from The Soul Swiper" at the fed's new arena in Library, PA, 16 January 1996.

how: Rolled up champion The Soul Swiper for the pin, 16 January 1996.
note: The same newsletter foreshadows a title defense against The Executioner two days later, which the record shows he lost.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-world
label: The Executioner

won.source: The fed's own "Friday Newsletter" (21 January 1996): "The Executioner won the WWCF World title belt from Masked Mayhem" at a house show in Gatlinburg, TN, 18 January 1996.

how: Defeated champion Masked Mayhem with a guillotine maneuver, 18 January 1996.
note: The same newsletter's own official card for the fed's first pay-per-view ("WWCF's Midnight Raid," 20 January 1996) lists The Executioner defending against The Hitman; that show's own results do not survive in the held record.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-world
label: Masked Mayhem

won.source: Already billed as champion in the fed's own first surviving newsletter (12 January 1996 dateline): "the champion Masked Mayhem met the talented Hitman" -- no earlier title-change document survives in the held record.

how: Already champion when the fed's own surviving record begins.
note: Lost the title to The Hitman on the fed's first recorded house-show date, 9 January 1996.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-intercontinental
label: Tecker

won.source: The fed's own "Saturday Newsletter" (12 January 1996): "Tecker beat Robbie 'Boston' Cooper for the Intercontinental Championship," 9 January 1996, with interference from Jamie Cutlass and manager Bobby Heenan.

how: Pinned champion Robbie "Boston" Cooper after outside interference, 9 January 1996.
note: The same newsletter's own next section has the title changing to a different named wrestler two days later, an internal inconsistency the fed's own text does not resolve; that section's itemized quick-results line, more consistent with the rest of the newsletter's own bookkeeping, instead has Tecker retaining the belt from Shawn Michaels on 11 January 1996 (a draw). Tecker went on to survive a disqualification challenge from Void MacLane, 16 January 1996 (titles do not change hands on a disqualification per the fed's own rules), before losing the belt on 18 January 1996.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-intercontinental
label: "The Fantasy" Brett Young

won.source: The fed's own "Friday Newsletter" (21 January 1996): "Brett Young won the WWCF Intercontinental belt from Tecker" at a house show in Gatlinburg, TN, 18 January 1996, after his manager distracted the referee.

how: Defeated champion Tecker with a foreign object after a manager distraction, 18 January 1996.
note: Still recognized as champion when the surviving record breaks off, 21 January 1996.

title: wwcf-weizal-1996-intercontinental
label: Robbie "Boston" Cooper

won.source: Billed as defending "his newly earned gold" in the fed's own first surviving newsletter (12 January 1996); no title-change document for how he won it survives in the held record.

how: Already champion when the fed's own surviving record begins.
note: Lost the title to Tecker at the fed's first house show, 9 January 1996, by manager and outside interference.
